verdict: TURSO REJECTED FOR UETGPT'S PRIMARY VECTOR STORE
reason: Tested DiskANN configurations failed the required combination of retrieval quality, build behavior, and operational recoverability.
scope_note: This verdict is narrow and specific to the exact DiskANN configurations tested (diskann_f8 and diskann_f16, on a synthetic 768-dim clustered-random corpus at scales 1000/5000/10000/20652, against a libSQL/Turso Cloud database in aws-ap-south-1). It does NOT claim 'Turso cannot store 20,652 vectors' as a general proposition - that broader claim was never tested and is not asserted here. Raw storage capacity was separately modeled (see incident-diskann-001.json storageModel) and was not the failure mode.

supporting_facts.fact: Ground truth (exact cosine, brute force) over the full real-scale row count of 20,652 vectors was deterministic, duplicate-free, row-count-matched, with latency p50=228ms / p95=259ms / p99=284ms (n=30 samples).
diskann_f8 at scale=1000: PASS. Recall@5=1.000, Recall@10=1.000, Recall@20=1.000. Build 134,183ms. Storage 70,246,400 bytes index-only (70,246 bytes/vector).
diskann_f8 at scale=5000: PASS. Recall@5=1.000, Recall@10=1.000, Recall@20=0.988. Build 579,378ms. Storage 351,215,616 bytes index-only (70,243 bytes/vector).

diskann_f8 at scale=10000: CONDITIONAL - FAILS the pre-declared Recall@10 >= 0.98 gate. Recall@5=0.953, Recall@10=0.963, Recall@20=0.967. Build 1,413,046ms (~23.5 min). Storage 702,345,216 bytes index-only (70,235 bytes/vector).

diskann_f8 at scale=20652 (the real production corpus size): FAIL. Build failed after 1,803,472ms (~30 min) with CLIENT_TIMEOUT: fetch failed. No integrity/recall/latency/storage/cleanup could be executed as a result. Table bench_diskann_f8_20652 may contain partial/orphaned structures; deliberately not auto-cleaned per incident containment policy.
supporting_facts.classification: EXECUTED (build attempt) / NOT_EXECUTED (all downstream measurements, because the build itself did not complete)
supporting_facts.gate_result: FAIL (reliability gate: build did not complete at production scale)

supporting_facts.fact: diskann_f16 at scale=1000: PASS. Recall@10=1.000. Build 190,957ms. Storage 135,200,768 bytes index-only (135,201 bytes/vector).
diskann_f16 at scale=5000: PASS (against the 0.98 gate). Recall@5=0.993, Recall@10=0.987, Recall@20=0.990. Build 1,445,949ms (~24 min). Storage 675,954,688 bytes index-only (135,191 bytes/vector).

diskann_f16 at scale=10000: FAIL. Build failed after 1,803,526ms (~30 min) with CLIENT_TIMEOUT: fetch failed. f16 was consequently never attempted at the full 20,652 scale, since it had already failed at a smaller scale.
supporting_facts.classification: EXECUTED (build attempt) / NOT_EXECUTED (20652 scale, and all downstream measurements at 10000)
supporting_facts.gate_result: FAIL (reliability gate: build did not complete even at 10,000, well short of production scale)

supporting_facts.fact: A separate, earlier incident (turso-default-diskann-fullscale-build-failure, status OPEN) occurred when building an uncompressed DiskANN index at the full 20,652 scale: the build failed with 'unable to update global metadata table', root-cause-assessed as LIKELY_SIGNIFICANT self-inflicted (a blind retry wrapper was applied uniformly to all client.execute/batch calls, including CREATE INDEX DDL; a second attempt collided with a still-in-flight or partially-committed first attempt). This left orphaned shadow-table structures (bench_default_uncompressed_idx_shadow and its index) that resisted 2 cleanup attempts (~5 min each, FAILED_OR_TIMED_OUT), forcing a containment decision to preserve them as forensic evidence and never touch that table again rather than a clean rollback.
supporting_facts.classification: EXECUTED / MEASURED, self-disclosed by the artifact as reconstructed-after-restart (facts unchanged, not re-derived) - see incident-diskann-001.json's own 'note' field
supporting_facts.gate_result: Contributes to operational-recoverability failure, but is explicitly NOT the sole basis for REJECTED - the clean re-run (after fixing the retry bug) still failed to complete a build at full scale in either compression mode, which is the primary, code-fix-independent basis for rejection.

supporting_facts.fact: After the retry-collision bug was fixed (CREATE INDEX routed through a no-retry executeOnce()), a re-test at n=5000 still required client fetch timeouts extended to 20-30 minutes (via undici setGlobalDispatcher) to complete, versus a default client timeout of approximately 5 minutes. This is a genuine, code-fix-independent finding: default client/library timeouts are insufficient for DiskANN index builds at this corpus scale, with direct implications for any production architecture that would need to build or rebuild this index synchronously.
supporting_facts.gate_result: Independently corroborates the reliability/build-behavior failure mode seen in the clean full ladder run.

gate_failures.requirement: Recall@10 >= 0.98 vs exact cosine ground truth
gate_failures.result: FAIL at scale=10000 for diskann_f8 (measured 0.963); scale=20652 (the real production size) never produced a measurable result for either config because the index build itself did not complete
FAIL - index build did not complete at production scale (20,652 vectors) for diskann_f8, and did not complete even at 10,000 vectors for diskann_f16, within a 30-minute client timeout

not_claimed: That Turso/libSQL cannot physically store 20,652 vectors (storage capacity was modeled separately and was not the observed failure mode)
That every possible DiskANN parameterization or a non-DiskANN approach would necessarily fail the same way (only diskann_f8, diskann_f16, and default_uncompressed were tested)

That the CLIENT_TIMEOUT failures prove a hard server-side limit rather than a client-configuration limit (the postFixFindings n5000 retest shows the same class of build DOES complete given a sufficiently extended client timeout at smaller scale; whether comparable extension would eventually succeed at the full 20,652 scale was not tested to completion and is not claimed either way)
fallback_action_per_gate_33: Per the pre-existing fallback sequence (acceptance-gates.json, section 33), Zilliz Cloud was then evaluated as the next candidate - see ../zilliz/verdict.json.
